speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what are the typical reasons given by households for not collecting the Bloobox; (b) what is the feedback given by households that have collected the Bloobox regarding its usefulness for their recycling efforts; (c) what are the measurable targets that NEA has set to determine the success of the Bloobox initiative; and (d) what will the Ministry do with uncollected boxes after the deadline for collection on 30 April 2023 has lapsed.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I will also respond to Question No 27 for written reply raised by Mr Melvin Yong and Question No 28 for written reply raised by Dr Wan Rizal from the Order Paper on 8 May 2023.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Bloobox initiative was launched in November 2022 as part of our national Recycle Right campaign.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Blooboxes carry labels to help households identify what can and cannot be recycled.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: By facilitating and encouraging households to set up a recycling corner, we hope to encourage recycling and raise the recycling rate.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To facilitate the distribution of Blooboxes, vending machines were placed across Singapore, including at community clubs and bus interchanges.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Distribution booths were also set up at community events, shopping malls and hawker centres.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These distribution efforts were publicised through flyers, posters and digital notifications via the Singpass mobile application.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Blooboxes were also distributed to interested primary and secondary schools to encourage students to recycle in school and at home.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The strong and positive response by the public reflects the community's interest in recycling at home or offices, and their appreciation of the utility of the Blooboxes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Following the end of the Bloobox distribution period, the National Environment Agency (NEA) will continue to collaborate with our various partners to encourage households to recycle as part of the Recycle Right campaign.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Do areas where there is a higher percentage of Blooboxes collected, have a higher recyclables collection rate?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: On a related note, for these areas, is there a higher percentage of recyclables that can actually be recycled that are not contaminants?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I would need to check whether we have micro data at the level of the estates or neighbourhoods, according to what the Member has asked for, based on the rate of the Bloobox collection.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The effort to promote recycling as well as recycling right is one that is ongoing and long term.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, this is one of the many initiatives that NEA has done and will be doing over time.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We thank the Member for his interest and to get his residents to do more recycling.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As for the Blooboxes, if there are members of the public who would like to have access to Blooboxes after the deadline, do look out for the various recycling initiatives by NEA and our partners, as that is where members of the public can have access to the Blooboxes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: If the Member is interested to promote recycling as a community, NEA would be happy to work with him to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Just a quick follow-up to the Member Yip Hon Weng's question.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue our efforts to promote recycling in the community.
